## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Nirodhavāra* ("Cessation section", Ya 2.2.2) is a section of the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka. Within the *Yamaka*, doctrinal categories across its various treatises are systematically examined in a "process section" (*pavattivāra*), which is regularly subdivided into three functional treatments: origination (*uppādavāra*), cessation (*nirodhavāra*), and combined origination and cessation (*uppādanirodhavāra*) [Anderson 1999; Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. Modern scholars note that these process sections in the *Yamaka* reflect early Buddhist process metaphysics—treating experience through processes across time (present, past, and future) rather than substantial entities—and mark a foundational milestone in the development of the Abhidhamma theory of momentariness (*khaṇa*), particularly the distinction between moments of arising (*uppādakkhaṇa*) and passing away (*bhaṅgakkhaṇa*) [Anderson 1999; Gal 2003; Nyanatiloka 2007; Ronkin 2005].
